Review: When you've got skin that tears easily, adhesive removers are an absolute necessity for any medical process.  I can't wear a regular bandaid or sensitive medical tape without causing micro tears on my skin and I keep skin adhesive remover in my purse for exactly this reason.  My favorite adhesive remover had been FreeDerm which was a siloxane product, but it's been impossible for me to source and keep in stock in the last year, so I've been on the hunt for another silicone based adhesive remover.  Was really excited to try this because it is a silicone based remover which means it won't sting or smell and works really great to dissolve hydrocolloid and other gooey adhesives quickly.  My son, who also has my same delicate skin condition, has to get EKGs regularly, this makes removal of the electrode patches significantly less miserable and we're able to get them off quickly without irritating his skin.  For adhesive patches that had to stay on longer, I did find I needed to let the spray sit for 2-3 minutes before it really would move easily.This has a wide spray area which is helpful for large areas covered by adhesive, but since I use this regularly to remove smaller adhesive patches, I did feel like I didn't have as much control over how much product was being used like I do with my old FreeDerm pump spray (though I did have to use more FreeDerm to get the same quick release, so in the end it might have been about the same amount of product being used).  I also used to spray between the adhesive patch being removed and the skin so that it would release while pulling the bandage off, but that's harder to do with this spray top since it sprays so much.  It probably is perfect for an adult managing a large site, but because these silicone based removers are so much more expensive than the solvent based removers, I don't want to waste a drop and would like to see this in either a spray pump or a more controlled spray option to use on kids with smaller treatment areas.  I will have to pick up the wipes to see if they're as effective as the spray because that may be my happy middle ground.  I don't use this to clean up adhesive residue which I find works better with one of the more traditional skin adhesive removers, this just makes removal of the initial bandage painless and easy (which often leaves less residue on the skin in the first place) and is ideal if you have to frequently change adhesive covers or medical devices.EDIT: I TRIED THE WIPES!  They're great, they don't work as well for removing electrodes because they can't soak through the backside of the electrode, so we're going to continue using the spray for electrode removal.  The wipes though are very nice and are now part of my regular first aid kit because they make removing bandages and tape MUCH easier and I can keep them in my purse for any scenario.  They also do a really good job removing adhesive residue from bandages that were left in place for a little too long. I'm happy to have found both of these because they each do a slightly different thing that we really need in our home with our family's skin conditions.

Review Title: Good Product for Me to Keep on Hand
Review: I learned after having an extensive surgery many years ago that I have a strong reaction to just about all types of medical tape. The adhesive material causes my skin to redden and blister, and after repeated dressing changes, my skin becomes a painful, raw mess. While there are hypoallergenic paper tapes, those tapes don't adhere very well, and there are times where the stronger, stickier tapes are a medical necessity. While I can't always avoid the adhesive material altogether, I find that the sooner I remove it in its entirety, the better my skin does. Since some surgeries are the result of medical emergencies and not planned in advance, I try to always have a supply of medical grade adhesive remover on hand in my home medical supplies. I try to keep both wipes and sprays, and was very happy to see this ConvaTec Esenta Adhesive Remover Spray available on amazon. I did a quick test of it with some surgical tape on my inner forearm, and am pleased with how well the spray removed any residual from the tape adhesive.

Review: I have seen a number of reviews critical of this product.  Not all adhesive removers are created equal.  Safe and Simple contains a water-based remover. Review: I've been using these for a few years now until I found out they are toxic. The ingredients listed on the box are "C10-11 Isoparaffin, Isopropyl Alcohol, Dipropylene Glycol Methyl Ether, Aloe Extract, Fragrance". While none of these are cancerogenic, the box has a pictogram of a "Health Hazard" in addition to "Flame" and "Acute Toxicity".If you look hard enough, you'll see that the product page has California’s Proposition 65 warning on it. it states the product contains "benzene", which is a well-known carcinogen that has been linked to leukemia and other cancers when humans are exposed to it over time. I'm not sure why this isn't directly written on the box. Benzene is commonly found as a contaminant in petroleum-based products or solvents used during the manufacturing process of various chemical ingredients. Although not directly listed, its presence might be in trace amounts in isoparaffins or isopropyl alcohol used in the wipes. This explains the strong odor other reviews have mentioned. DO NOT INHALE IT. As the warnings on the box state, use in a ventilated area.For now, I'm switching to another product that doesn't have a pictogram or Prop 65 warning. The lack of warning doesn't necessarily mean the product isn't exposed to benzene but it's best to avoid that do have warnings.

Review Title: Doesn’t help much on our cat’s Freestyle Libre 2 sensor removal
Review: I got this specifically to help remove the expired Freestyle Libre 2 sensors from our elderly cat, reading about someone using it similarly in the reviews before purchase. As far as I can tell on 2 attempts, it doesn’t seem to do anything really for this purpose and smells a little unpleasant. (Maybe the other review was talking about removing just the glue residue remaining on the cat from an already removed sensor, dunno.)The vet techs are glueing the sensors on, and the sticker part is apparently waterproof, or so I read elsewhere. I had been using a butter knife dipped in olive oil around the edges and waiting until the sticker lifted some and then repeating the process again and again, an undesirably long and tedious process, so I wanted a glue remover to get the sensor/sticker off in one attempt to be done with it. This product didn’t achieve that. It didn’t even seem to free up the plastic sensor much from the sticker itself, whereas with the olive oil and a day or so later, I could at least take the plastic sensor off enabling me to better and more thoroughly get the olive oil under parts of the remaining sticker that were loosened.I was just trying this product again and went back to the olive oil. I don’t know if using this product not in pad/wipe form but in straight liquid form would yield better results. I don’t know if using it on a younger cat or a cat whose shaved fur at the sensor placement might grow in faster would yield better results, but on our cat, the sticker is glued to skin where very little fur grows out in the 2 weeks the sensor lasts before it needs removing.If you have a cat who, like our cat, doesn’t mess with the sensor or who can wear the sensor without issue for 2 weeks, I would suggest you have them use less glue… and also not glue the very edge of the perimeter so you can get some oil or your choice of pet-safe solvent under the sticker to help in getting it back off when the time comes. Our cat is only on his 3rd sensor, and he literally would have 3 on him right now if I didn’t keep at this project of trying to remove the expired ones. (Thanks also to my husband who came up with the brilliant idea of using a permanent marker to put a mark on the expired one when the new one is put on so you can make sure you’re on the right sensor for both readings and removal attempts.)

Review Title: These are more economical than the bottle of Unisolve
Review: I have been using Uni-Solve Liquid Adhesive Remover for years. Review Title: You really want this product if you wear a CGM
Review: The adhesive that holds the CGM sensor on your body is good and strong, which is an advantage when you want to keep the CGM sensor on your body, and a disadvantage when you want to take it off.  When it comes time to take it off, this stuff is a real godsend.  You squeeze a little on the area around the CGM and then give it time to work... maybe 30 seconds. Review: I use insulin pump infusion sets and I have to change them every 3 days to prevent infection. Lets say that's a "recommendation" and sometimes this extends to 4 or 5 days... I am a busy man, what can I say. Anyhow, during this time, the adhesive on the sets sometimes gets very sticky and messy, and attracts dirt like a jar of honey to a hungry bear. It is like a dust and dirt magnet, forming a disgusting ring of black mess around the outside when you peel the set off... not to mention that the peeling the set off part is a painful mess of an encounter (I am a part middle-eastern man, with middle-eastern hair on my middle-eastern stomach, which can sometimes make the removal process a painful experience. Yes, I know, probably not as bad as a Brazilian, but come on... this is happening every few days here!)When I read about these wipes I was intrigued, because for all the time I have been using an insulin pump I was just told to use baby oil to remove the adhesive... which works to an extent, but can also be a messy experience (especially on hair.) Enter these wipes. A quick swab around the outside of the infusion set is enough to unseat it from its death grip on your skin, and makes it easy to peel a side of it off... then continuing to wipe as you peel it unlocks it from your skin without any pain whatsoever. Any hairs in the way stay rooted and the entire thing just comes off without any mess. Then a quick swab around the circumference of where the set was removes any built up gunk and/or dust and dirt that was shellacked to your skin only moments ago. It is extremely gentle and does not burn or sting, and I was able to wipe over top of the open hole where the cannula was without any pain or discomfort.These things are awesome. They smell strange, but its not nearly as bad as everyone is making it out to be. It's a sort of sweet chemically smell, almost akin to antifreeze. Not that bad when you consider how magical these things really are... I am noticing much less irritation around previous infusion set locations and am noticing much less pain when inserting new infusion sets over areas where the adhesive had to be scrubbed off in the shower previously.If you are hesitant about buying these for any reason, do yourself a favor and try a box. It will change your perspective on removing infusion sets. Looking back after trying these things, I have been to the hospital a couple times needing IV fluids and I cannot believe they don't use these at hospitals. They are so inexpensive and it would make removing IV dressings so much less painful! I might even keep some in my wallet just in case I get into an accident or something.

Review Title: Cancer Patient Approved for EKG Glue Removal
Review: Cancer patient here! This product easily removed all my stubborn EKG sticker glue! After a week of scrubbing I still couldn’t get the glue residue off completely...and then I got all new stickers changed out so I had more to worry about during my multiple hospital stays. I kept asking for some kind of remover but the hospital only had small alcohol wipes which didn’t work so I went hunting on amazon. The actual package inside the box was dinged up and I was worried if it was repackaged or not, but I still opened them because I was desperate. These wipes worked like magic! So happy with them. I have sensitive skin too but no problems. It only burned on one area where my skin was previously irritated, it did not burn or sting on any other spots. It does leaves a bit of a residue but drys quickly and leaves skin soft. I recommend using before the shower so you can get all the glue off and not worry about the residue feeling (if your like me, but again it drys quickly and isn’t sticky). It still takes a little scrubbing but these worked very well. Definitely worth buying for the cheap price for 50 wipes. For reference I only used 2 wipes to get about 6 glue patches off so these should last a while.
